This provision does not comply with Ind AS 37 as there are no present obligation arising from a past event established, the amount is not a best estimate of any identifiable outflow, but a number calibrated to the size of the company. Notes fail to disclose nature of obligation, expected timing of outflows, or basis of estimation. outlook.statement: The long-term outlook for Indian manufacturing remains encouraging. The Company will continue to focus on operational efficiencies, supply chain resilience, and expanding its customer base in international markets.

Global textile and apparel industry expected to gradually recover as inflationary pressures moderate, consumer demand improves and global inventory levels normalise; pace of recovery likely to vary across regions.

Long-term fundamentals of Indian textile sector remain positive supported by favourable demographics, expanding domestic consumption, government initiatives promoting manufacturing and exports, and increasing investments across the textile value chain.
Latex rubber thread industry expected to benefit from higher consumption levels as demand from domestic and international garment manufacturers improves.

Long-term outlook for Indian tissue paper industry remains encouraging supported by increasing awareness of hygiene and wellness, rising disposable incomes, urbanisation, growth of hospitality and healthcare sectors, expansion of organised retail and increasing consumer preference for convenience-oriented products.
Industry witnessing gradual shift towards environmentally responsible products and sustainable manufacturing practices; Premier committed to aligning operations with these expectations.
Digital commerce and quick-commerce platforms opening new avenues for product accessibility and consumer engagement; Premier expects digital sales to become increasingly important contributor.

Premier Tissues well positioned to capitalise on significant growth opportunities in Indian tissue paper industry with recognised brand, expanding distribution network, ongoing capacity enhancement, commitment to sustainability and operational excellence.

Outlook for global textile and apparel industry remains cautiously optimistic; long-term fundamentals positive; India well positioned to benefit from supply-chain diversification, sustainability trends, and India-EU FTA; natural rubber industry expected to remain sensitive to supply-side constraints and climatic conditions; global natural rubber demand projected firm in 2026 with moderate production increase but susceptible to disruptions and price volatility; Premier Tissues expects long-term growth from hygiene awareness, urbanisation, rising incomes, organised retail, hospitality, healthcare, food-service; per capita tissue consumption in India substantially below developed markets indicating headroom; capacity expansion planned to improve manufacturing flexibility and supply capabilities.
